headline: Iran oil facilities attacked - global supply at risk
summary: Reports of strikes on Iranian oil facilities raise concerns about potential supply disruptions in the Middle East, pushing crude oil prices up sharply.

nodes.label: Iran
nodes.description: Major oil-producing nation and OPEC member; direct exposure to the attack.

nodes.label: Crude Oil
nodes.description: Global benchmark energy commodity; price-sensitive to Middle East supply shocks.

nodes.label: Energy Sector
nodes.description: Producers, refiners and integrated oil companies.

nodes.label: Transportation
nodes.description: Airlines, shipping and logistics where fuel is a major operating cost.

nodes.label: Manufacturing
nodes.description: Industrial producers exposed to higher energy and input costs.

nodes.label: Inflation Expectations

nodes.label: USA

edges.explanation: Attacks on oil facilities may reduce exportable supply, tightening global crude balances.
limitations: Actual supply loss depends on damage severity, which is not confirmed.

edges.explanation: Higher crude prices help upstream producers but raise input costs for refiners and downstream energy users.
Fuel is a large operating cost for airlines, shipping and logistics; higher fuel prices compress margins.
limitations: Hedging and fuel surcharges can delay the cost pass-through.

edges.explanation: Energy-intensive manufacturers face higher input costs when energy prices rise.
limitations: Energy intensity varies widely across sub-sectors.

edges.explanation: Higher energy prices feed into headline inflation and inflation expectations.
limitations: Pass-through depends on how long prices stay elevated.

edges.explanation: Rising inflation expectations can push market-implied policy rates higher.
limitations: Central banks may look through temporary energy shocks.

edges.explanation: Higher rates can help net-interest margins but hurt credit demand and asset quality.
limitations: Net effect depends on balance-sheet composition.

edges.explanation: Higher financing costs weigh on property demand and valuations.
limitations: Effects typically lag by several quarters.

edges.explanation: US producers benefit from higher prices; consumers and fuel-heavy sectors face higher costs.
limitations: Net effect depends on the balance of production and consumption.

edges.explanation: India is heavily import-dependent on crude; higher prices widen the trade deficit and pressure the currency.
limitations: Pass-through depends on domestic fuel pricing policy.

edges.explanation: China imports large volumes of crude but has diversified suppliers and strategic reserves.
The EU is energy-import dependent; higher prices feed inflation and complicate ECB policy.
limitations: Gas and oil effects are different channels and are not separated here.
